description: We are Astra 6, tackling the abandoned space exploration equipment challenge on the Moon and Mars. Our team is passionate about space sustainability, robotics, and innovative engineering. We are looking for motivated teammates skilled in coding, 3D modeling, aerospace research, or UI/UX design. Join us to turn discarded lunar and Martian hardware into useful future mission resources! Contact us via Discord: Anamikas
summary: "Still Out There" is a kid-friendly website telling the stories of 11 pieces of NASA hardware left on the Moon, Mars and deep space. Each card shows what it was, the science it made possible, and where it is now, with a quiz at the end. It meets the challenge by explaining this hardware simply for school-age students, and it matters because it shows that exploration continues, with every fact linked to NASA.
details: Still Out There is a free, kid-friendly website that tells the stories of 11 pieces of NASA hardware left on the Moon, on Mars and in deep space, such as the Apollo rover, Curiosity and the Voyagers. Each story card explains in simple words what the equipment was, what science it made possible and where it is now, with a Silent or Still working badge, a NASA picture and a link to the NASA page behind the facts. The site has Moon, Mars and Deep Space pages joined by one menu, and ends with a 5-question quiz that counts the score. It works in any browser, including phones, needs no sign-up, and lets students and teachers check every fact on NASA's own pages. We hope it makes young learners curious and shows them that exploration is still going on. We built it with HTML, CSS and JavaScript in VS Code, worked together using Git and GitHub, and hosted it on GitHub Pages. We made it creative by turning each machine into a short story with a clear status badge and a quiz. We considered accuracy, a child-friendly audience, easy access, fair teamwork with one page file per member, and NASA image credit.
